transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-10-07
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sara Kim (CTO - Orion), David Ruiz (ML Eng - Orion), Priya Nair (Platform - Orion)

Summary:
Quick scoping to agree on POC success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, and timeline/milestones (kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, exec readout). Agreed to SOW and security docs next steps, kickoff 10/14, initial benchmark within first week after access.

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency, cost, quality/regression thresholds)
- Workload sizing (RPS, tokens per request, concurrency/peaks)
- Benchmark plan (baseline vs optimized runs, dataset, metrics)
- Timeline & milestones (kickoff, access, mid-point, exec readout)
- Security & access (VPN/VPC, SSO, audit logs, KMS)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time today. Quick intros, we got our SE Liam on the call, he'll drive the benchmark details.
[00:12] Sara: Hi all, Sara here, CTO at Orion. We're trying to validate cost & latency for a customer-facing assistant, and want a clear POC timeline so we can plan exec review.
[00:23] Liam: Great, thanks. David, can you say a bit about current traffic and workloads?
[00:30] David: Sure. Right now in prod-ish staging we see 120 rps steady with spikes to about 450 rps during peak. Typical request size is ~180 tokens input, we append about 70 tokens on average per response, so roughly 250 tokens total. We expect production to be similar but with higher peaks, maybe 600 rps peak if adoption grows.
[00:52] Priya: Important to add: all traffic must stay within our VPC for the POC, and we need SSO + audit logs. SOC2 is a checkbox for our security team.
[01:05] Maya: Understood. We can run the POC in Redwood Dedicated in your VPC or Redwood Private — both support SSO and KMS. For the timeline today, we'll assume staging access via peered VPC or read-only bastion.
[01:18] Sara: Sounds good. What success criteria should we anchor on? Latency p95? cost per 1M tokens? quality/relevance thresholds?
[01:27] Liam: From experience a typical enterprise POC has 3 pillars: 1) latency SLO (p95 under 700ms for 256 token end-to-end is typical for our infra with batching), 2) throughput/cost — e.g., cost per 1M tokens below your target (we can model with the SOW), and 3) quality/accuracy — no more than 10% regression on your key evaluation prompts compared to current baseline. We should codify exact numbers for Orion.
[01:48] David: For us latency p95 under 500ms would be ideal, but we'll accept up to 700ms for initial testing. Cost target is less clear, we need Redwood to show cost per 1M tokens and recommendations (quantization, batching).
[02:02] Maya: We'll surface model/quantization recommendations in the SOW and in the benchmark results. We'll run baseline unquantized + one quantized run.
[02:12] Liam: Benchmark plan I'd propose: 1) Baseline run using your sample dataset (we'll ingest 50k typical requests) for 24-48 hours, capture p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, error rates, token accounting, and cost estimate; 2) Optimization run with recommended batching/quantization profiles; 3) Stress test for peak concurrency to validate autoscaling. We'll share a spreadsheet template for metrics. Link: drive.link/orion-bench (placeholder).
[02:43] Priya: For access, we'll provide a read-only IAM role and a peered VPC endpoint. Can Redwood run the agents from their side with the peered endpoint?
[02:52] Liam: Yes, we can run our benchmark controller in your VPC via a temporary bastion. We'll need a small firewall rule and a service account.
[03:01] Sara: Ok. Timeline? We need an exec readout to leadership around 11/04, so what's realistic?
[03:07] Maya: Proposed milestones: Kickoff (10/14), Access & environment provisioning (by 10/17), Baseline benchmark and initial report (by 10/21), Mid-point technical review (10/28) to iterate on optimizations, Finalized benchmark and cost model (11/01), Exec readout (11/04). That fits a ~3-week deep POC.
[03:28] David: That timeline looks fine but we need the SOW and a clear list of what we must provision.
[03:33] Maya: We'll send SOW + checklist. Also will include an explicit security pack (SOC2 evidence, network diagrams, KMS options).
[03:41] Priya: A couple of constraints: data residency — logs must remain in us-west-2 and the customer data must not persist after POC; and encryption keys must be customer-managed if possible.
[03:52] Liam: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Redwood Private and Dedicated. We can configure log forwarding to your SIEM and ensure audit logs are retained according to your policy. We'll note retention controls in the SOW.
[04:06] Sara: On benchmarks, we want to validate both conversation style prompts and single-turn completions. We'll provide a split of sample payloads.
[04:15] Liam: Good call — we'll run separate slices: short-turn (<64 tokens), mid-turn (~250 tokens), and long-turn (~800 tokens) to capture different performance characteristics. For batching effects we'll model the mix you provide.
[04:29] David: Any expected differences if we run Redwood Dedicated vs hosted? We prefer Dedicated for SLA.
[04:34] Maya: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; hosted can be faster to start but may have noisier tails during peak multi-tenant events. For POC Dedicated in your VLAN is ideal since you care about residency and keys. We'll outline cost delta in the SOW.
[04:47] Sara: Competitor question — we've talked to ApexAI and CloudModel. They gave us quick numbers but no clear kernel-level optimization advice. We want to see tangible perf improvements.
[04:56] Liam: We'll include a kernel/quantization plan and expected unit-cost impact. For example, quantizing to int8 can reduce GPU memory footprint and cost by ~25% in many workloads, but we'll validate quality via your eval set.
[05:10] Maya: To recap milestones and owners: Kickoff (10/14) - Maya to schedule; Access setup (by 10/17) - David/Priya to provision; Baseline benchmark (10/21) - Liam to run and report; Mid-point review (10/28) - technical deep-dive; Exec readout (11/04) - Sara to lead with Redwood presenting results.
[05:30] Priya: Action items noted. Please include exact firewall rules in the checklist; our security team will stamp it.
[05:36] Liam: Will do. Also we'll provide a benchmark runbook and scripts so you can re-run locally.
[05:42] David: One more: can we include an A/B with our current model for quality comparison?
[05:47] Maya: Yes, include your baseline endpoints and we'll annotate evaluation scores against that baseline.
[05:52] Sara: Great. Any blockers we haven't covered?
[05:56] Priya: Only getting the SOW and security pack in time. If we get those by Friday we'll be on schedule.
[06:02] Maya: We'll get SOW + security pack out by 2025-10-09.
[06:07] Sara: Thanks, sounds good.
[06:10] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with calendar invites and links to the drive doc.

End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional word substitution, some speaker labels simplified; timestamps are approximate.
